title: Wagon cup holder: v6.1, standard M4 hardware
subtitle: Clip stays on the side rail · cup module lifts off its dovetail · clamped by an ordinary M4 screw, washer and nut · shown assembled in its real orientation (rail left to right, cup upright) · millimetres
scale_note: Real size, shown assembled in its real orientation: the rail runs left to right, the cup stands upright and hangs off the outside of it. The rail is your 22.3 mm tube. The tumbler is from retailer listings (70 mm base, 89 mm widest). The two wireframe blocks are the red latch and diagonal strut at each end of your 120 mm clear stretch. They are APPROXIMATE: only the ~26 mm reach is from you, and I assumed they sit only beyond the clear stretch.
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v6.1: most hobby kits stop short of a 40 mm bolt, so the clip is redesigned around ordinary M4 hardware. The screw head and washer now sit recessed in the inboard ear and the nut in the outboard ear, each in a 5 mm deep pocket with a 3 mm wall behind it. That shortens the run, so an M4 x 30 works (it engages 2.5 of the nut's 3.2 mm) and an M4 x 35 engages it fully. The ears are 8 mm thick now, so the clip hangs 3.5 mm less below the rail. The ring, mouth, dovetail and the whole cup module are unchanged, so only the clip needs reprinting. The screw, washer and nut are shown in place. Please check: (1) what is the longest M4 screw in your kit? (2) is there room for the screw head and a 3 mm hex key on the inboard side? (3) the old checks still stand: the strut under the cup, and folding.
